_readme: IMP-11. Exceptions to check-dead-machinery.mjs, each with a reason someone
can evaluate later. This is a record of decisions, not a mute button.
A reason beginning with 'KNOWN GAP' means the thing genuinely is not wired
up yet. Those are counted and reported separately on every run, so unfinished
work stays visible in the check's own output instead of being silenced by
being written down. Clear them by wiring the thing up, not by editing the
reason.
The gap count jumped on 2026-07-31. It was not a new outbreak: rule 1 was
counting TypeScript COMMENTS as callers and rule 3 could not fire at all.
Everything added that day was already in this state and invisible, and each
entry was checked against the live database before being written down.
A fourth group, function_overloads, was added on 2026-07-31. Postgres
identifies a function by name AND argument types, so one name can be two
functions — skip_visit was, for a month, and rule 1 could not see the dead
one because the live one had callers. An entry here means an overload set is
deliberate and says which signatures are meant. There are none today.
unwired_server_fns is EMPTY as of 2026-08-07 and should stay that way.
It held 28 entries under one shared reason saying they had not been
individually investigated. They have been now: 24 were deleted (each a
duplicate of a wired path, a writer for a superseded column, or the
remains of a screen that was never built) and 4 were wired up. Two of
them were doing real harm while dormant — chargeInvoiceWithSavedCard
would have charged a card without applying account credit first, and
generateAddonCharges being unreachable meant recurring add-ons produced
no charges at all. A new entry here needs its own reason, not a shared one.

endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/calendar.$token.ts: Subscribed-calendar feed. Polled by Google Calendar, Apple Calendar and Outlook from their own servers, at the URL a person copies from the Calendar feed card (Profile, Settings -> Scheduling); nothing in src/ calls it and nothing should.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/hooks/announcement: Deliberately unscheduled, and no longer unreachable. The 120-line send moved to lib/announcement-emails.server, which a platform admin now invokes per announcement from /platform/announcements — so an announcement marked send_email actually gets sent, which it never did before. This endpoint stays as the shape a scheduler needs if the owner ever wants one; scheduling platform-wide outbound email is their decision, not a cleanup task. Both callers share a per-recipient idempotency key, so adding a cron later cannot double-send.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/hooks/live-activit: The iPhone app's StartStopIntent (ios/App/App/LiveActivity/RouteActivityIntents.swift), when a technician presses Start on the route's Live Activity on the lock screen. iOS runs the intent in the app's process with no web view, so the caller is Swift, not anything in src/; the URL it posts to is minted by src/components/my-day/RouteLockScreen.tsx (apiUrl(LIVE_ACTIVITY_ACTION_PATH)) and kept with the action token in the keychain.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/hooks/late-check.t: pg_cron job 'late-check', */5 * * * * — created by 20261007160000, and it only POSTs when public.late_check_due() says some open, assigned stop's window closes between two hours ago and three hours from now.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/hooks/platform-str: Stripe platform webhook endpoint, for HoundStack's own SaaS billing (bucket A).
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/hooks/qbo-callback: QuickBooks OAuth redirect target — the browser lands here after a tenant authorizes.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/hooks/stripe.ts: Stripe Connect webhook endpoint. Called by Stripe on tenant payment events.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/hooks/webhook-deli: pg_cron job 'deliver-webhooks', * * * * * — created by 20260929080000, and it only POSTs when the outbox has a delivery due.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/hooks/weekly-diges: pg_cron job 'weekly-digest', 0 13 * * 1 — created by 20260731130000, verified in cron.job.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/invoice-pdf.ts: A browser, from the 'Download PDF' link on the public pay page (src/routes/pay.i.$token.tsx), and from the office's Download PDF button in the native app, which opens it in the system browser sheet because a WKWebView cannot save a blob. The capability is invoices.public_token, the same as the pay page.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/leads.ts: Public lead-capture form, embedded on tenant websites. Called by a browser from outside the app.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/quote-pdf.ts: A browser, from the 'Download PDF' link on the public quote page (src/routes/q.$token.tsx), and from the office quote page's Download PDF button in the native app. Reads through public_quote_document, which answers nothing for a draft.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/verify-email.ts: Target of the verification link in a signup email.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/api/public/website-submission: Public contact and early-access forms on houndstack.com and www.houndstack.com. Called by a browser from the marketing site.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/email/auth/webhook.ts: Supabase Auth send-email hook — Supabase calls this to render auth mail.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/email/suppression.ts: Provider bounce/complaint webhook — writes the suppression list.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/email/transactional/send.ts: NO CALLER, and the previous reason here was wrong: it claimed the app's own notification code calls this server-to-server. It does not. Nothing in src/ references the path, and lib/email/enqueue.server.ts says outright that system code 'bypasses /email/transactional/send auth by writing directly to the pgmq queue'. The endpoint also requires a user Bearer JWT, which system code has none of. Kept because it is a reachable authenticated endpoint a future user-initiated send could use; the exemption now records that it is unused rather than pretending it is wired.
endpoint_callers.src/routes/email/unsubscribe.ts: Target of the List-Unsubscribe header and the footer link in every marketing email.

function_overloads.stop_service_min: Both signatures are meant. stop_service_min(integer, integer) is minutes on site from the service default, then the yard, then 8, and every older caller still uses it. stop_service_min(integer, integer, integer) prefers visits.duration_min when a groom stored a length, and otherwise calls the two-argument function. route_day_inputs and apply_route_plan were spliced in 20261016190000 to pass v.duration_min as the first argument. Neither signature has a defaulted parameter, so a two-argument call still reaches the older complete body rather than a truncated copy of the new one. A caller that wants the visit length has to pass three arguments.
function_overloads.staff_start_point: Both signatures are meant, and they answer the same question about different inputs. staff_start_point(uuid,uuid,date) resolves the start of a technician's day from what is ASSIGNED to them, and is what plan_route calls after plan_day_across_staff has written the assignments. staff_start_point(uuid,uuid,date,uuid[]) resolves it from a PLANNED set of visits, and is what plan_visits calls inside plan_day_across_staff_dryrun, which by design has written nothing there is to read. Tiers 1 and 2 of the chain (personal address, business location) are identical in both; only the disposal-site and periphery tiers differ, and after an apply the two agree by construction — that agreement is the point of the four-argument one and was measured on 2026-08-19 (preview 7/7/6 at 139.3/143.1/91.9 drive minutes, apply identical). The overload hazard this rule names — a caller omitting an argument and silently reaching the older body — is not live here: the three-argument version has no defaulted parameters and is a complete, correct answer for post-write callers, so an omission gets the right function rather than a truncated one. Added 20260815190000.

uncalled_rpcs.assign_route_for_day: Superseded by plan_route/optimize_route_v3. Its only caller was the legacy one-tech card, deleted in 20260805060000 along with the whole-day reassignment bug. EXECUTE is revoked from authenticated in that same migration, so it is unreachable rather than merely uncalled; the definition stays because the eligibility migration's record is written around it.
uncalled_rpcs.is_visit_tech: Called from ~10 SQL bodies in this tree and from the storage policy in 20260701161658. The previous reason claimed the scanner could not see it because bootstrap-dump policies are not files — but that policy IS a file, so the stated premise was false even though the exemption is harmless. Kept as a no-op guard against the scanner's SQL-body parsing regressing.

unreachable_modules.src/components/billing/PlanPicker.native: Reached by a BUILD-TIME ALIAS, not by an import, so no file under src/routes can name it and this check cannot see the edge. vite.config.ts resolves @/components/billing/PlanPicker to this file in a NATIVE_BUILD, so the HoundStack subscription purchase UI is absent from the store binary rather than merely gated inside it. Verified by build: stripeAppearance, which appears only in the real module, is in 0 chunks of dist-native. Parity with the real module's exports is pinned by tests/the-store-binary-does-not-carry-a-plan-picker.test.ts, because tsc follows tsconfig paths rather than vite aliases and would never notice a drift.
